body:
Spec: .adlc/specs/install-experience.md (I2 section is binding).

=== CONTEXT ===
Adoption today is at minimum `npx plugins add voodootikigod/adlc` + `npm i -g @adlc/cli` + a per-repo init, and the `plugins` installer only reliably covers Claude Code. The other six harnesses each have a divergent native path documented across six pages. There is no Windows story.

Unlike herdr (a static binary), ADLC is Node. The installer's hard prerequisite is Node >= 18 + npm; it detects and guides, it never bootstraps Node. That also makes Windows MORE tractable for ADLC than for herdr: packages/tickets already carries win32 branches. The real exclusion is packages/fleet, which hard-codes /bin/sh and POSIX sandbox backends.

A `curl | sh` served from our own domain is a supply-chain trust root. ADR-0009 accepted the `npx plugins` risk; this is a distinct decision and needs its own ADR.

Published on npm at 1.6.0: cli, core, opencode, pi, antigravity, cursor, codex. NOT published: @adlc/copilot, @adlc/herdr -- the installer must print their current native path rather than depend on unpublished packages.

=== TASK ===
1. Write `apps/docs/public/install.sh` in POSIX sh: check Node >= 18 (exit non-zero with an actionable message if absent/old, installing nothing), `npm install -g @adlc/cli`, detect each present harness (claude, codex, cursor, opencode, pi, agy, herdr, copilot) and run only that harness's native install, then print next steps ending at `adlc init`.
2. Write `apps/docs/public/install.ps1` as the Windows beta equivalent; it must contain the string "beta".
3. Add `test/install-sh.test.mjs` covering: `sh -n` syntax, the no-Node case, the detection case (stub PATH exposing a subset of harness binaries, all commands captured through a logging shim; assert every stubbed harness got its native command and no absent harness is named), idempotence (two runs, byte-equal command logs), the ps1 beta label, Windows honesty (every doc offering install.ps1 states `adlc fleet` is POSIX-only), and digest pinning against test/install-digests.json.
4. Add a `windows-latest` job to .github/workflows/ci.yml running the core package suites excluding packages/fleet, plus a PowerShell parse check of install.ps1. Make it a required check.
5. Write docs/adr/0010-first-party-curl-installer.md, Status Accepted, cross-referencing ADR-0009.
6. Document the installer in README.md and the integration guides, stating the Node prerequisite and the fleet/POSIX exclusion.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC2.1: `sh -n apps/docs/public/install.sh` exits 0. VERIFY: `node --test test/install-sh.test.mjs` syntax case passes.
- AC2.2: No Node on PATH => exit >= 1, stderr names Node 18, no npm invocation logged. VERIFY: `node --test test/install-sh.test.mjs` no-node case passes.
- AC2.3: Installs @adlc/cli and runs native installs for exactly the stubbed harnesses. VERIFY: `node --test test/install-sh.test.mjs` detection case passes.
- AC2.4: Second run exits 0 with a command log byte-equal to the first. VERIFY: `node --test test/install-sh.test.mjs` idempotence case passes.
- AC2.5: install.ps1 exists, contains "beta", and parses. VERIFY: `node --test test/install-sh.test.mjs` ps1 case passes and the windows-latest CI parse step is green.
- AC2.6: Core gates pass on Windows. VERIFY: the windows-latest job in .github/workflows/ci.yml is green and required.
- AC2.7: Editing either installer without updating test/install-digests.json fails the suite. VERIFY: `node --test test/install-sh.test.mjs` digest case passes, and the mutation is demonstrated to fail it.
- AC2.8: ADR recorded. VERIFY: `grep -q 'Status:\\*\\* \\*\\*Accepted' docs/adr/0010-first-party-curl-installer.md` exits 0.
- AC2.9: Every doc offering install.ps1 states `adlc fleet` is POSIX-only. VERIFY: `node --test test/install-sh.test.mjs` Windows-honesty case passes.

=== OUTCOME (P5, PR #351) ===
AC2.5 and AC2.6 WITHDRAWN. The windows-latest job written to back the Windows
beta claim is what refuted it: 6 of 28 core package suites passed. The shared
bin-resolution path builds D:\D:\... from an already-absolute Windows path.
install.ps1, the windows-core CI job, and scripts/windows-core-tests.mjs were
all removed before merge rather than shipping a beta label over a platform where
four fifths of the gates fail. Every surface now states Windows is unsupported
and points at WSL, and install-sh.test.mjs carries a tripwire asserting no .ps1
is served. Native Windows support is tracked separately.

The apps/docs/public/install.ps1 rail is retained deliberately: narrowing a rail
is privileged, and the declaration is a historical record of what this ticket
froze. The file is gone, so the rail is inert.
title: First-party one-command installer (install.sh + beta install.ps1) with harness detection and Windows CI
